answer: A dune-backed coast stays honest when every new identity must keep a distinct tide watch at a different shore station, recording the pulse of the tide by hand each hour through a full night while a distinct wharf clerk checks the log at dawn. The first fake owes one watch, the second two, the third four, doubling each time, so the tenth fake alone owes 512 nights and twenty fakes would owe over a million. Bulk farming fails because stations are few, tides never pause, and one keeper cannot stand on twenty shores in a single night, like a wharf that berths one boat per pier.
